description: We are Team ArtemisTwin —a multidisciplinary group of student developers, data engineers, and space enthusiasts brought together by the 2026 NASA International Space Apps Challenge. Combining expertise in algorithmic modeling, geospatial web development, and planetary science research, we built ArtemisTwin to make lunar and Martian field-site selection transparent, data-driven, and accessible to researchers worldwide.
summary: ArtemisTwin is an interactive, zero-backend planetary-analog screening engine built for the NASA International Space Apps Challenge to help mission planners match Earth environments to lunar and Martian landing zones. Before launching hardware, engineers rely on terrestrial test sites, but relying on visual guesswork creates costly blind spots. ArtemisTwin solves this by evaluating Earth windows across a 12-layer environmental framework—covering slope, thermal extremes, solar irradiance, and mineralogy—against authentic planetary target envelopes derived from NASA LRO LOLA, Diviner, and MGS MOLA archives. Users can compare canonical benchmark sites or drop a pin anywhere on Earth to stream live AWS Terrarium elevation tiles and NASA POWER climatology normals in the browser. The platform generates mission-weighted Analog Fit scores across four test profiles (Rover Mobility, Ice Detection, Habitat Thermal Test, and Cave Robotics) complete with 4,000-draw Monte Carlo confidence intervals and explicit physical gap tracking for unreplicable conditions like lunar vacuum. By replacing subjectivity with rigorous open data, ArtemisTwin makes analog testing smarter, safer, and fully transparent.
details:
Project Summary

Before launching rovers, habitats, or astronauts to the Moon or Mars, mission teams must validate hardware in harsh terrestrial environments. However, no single Earth desert or volcanic field mirrors space—and picking test sites by visual guesswork leads to costly blind spots.

ArtemisTwin replaces subjective intuition with a transparent, data-driven screening platform. It evaluates any Earth window across a 12-layer environmental framework—spanning slope, thermal extremes, solar irradiance, atmospheric pressure, and mineralogy—against authentic planetary target envelopes derived from NASA LRO LOLA, Diviner, and MGS MOLA archives.

Powered entirely client-side via live AWS elevation tiles, NASA POWER climatology normals, and NASA EONET hazard feeds, ArtemisTwin computes mission-weighted Analog Fit scores across four engineering profiles (Rover Mobility, Ice Detection, Habitat Thermal Test, and Cave Robotics). By running 4,000-draw Monte Carlo simulations, the platform delivers realistic  confidence bands and explicit physical gap warnings (such as lunar vacuum), empowering researchers to optimize field campaigns and make space exploration safer and smarter.

The Challenge & Motivation

Space exploration hardware requires rigorous terrestrial validation. Yet, relying on traditional analog sites chosen by tradition or visual likeness creates severe engineering risks. ArtemisTwin addresses this by establishing a rigorous, quantitative baseline for Earth-to-space site selection.

Architecture & Data Integration

ArtemisTwin is built as a fast, zero-backend, client-side web application that integrates multiple open-data ecosystems:

  • Planetary Mission Baselines: Utilizes static target envelopes derived from NASA LRO LOLA (topography/slope), LRO Diviner (lunar thermal extremes), and MGS MOLA / Mars Odyssey THEMIS (Martian topography and surface temperatures).
  • Live Earth Data & Elevation: Streams AWS Terrarium z14 elevation tiles (~12.5 m resolution) directly in the browser to compute Horn 33 slopes and 49-point East–West elevation profiles for any custom coordinate on Earth.
  • Climatology & Operational Safety: Integrates live multi-year MERRA-2 assimilation normals via the NASA POWER API (skin temperature, solar irradiance, pressure, wind speed) and active natural hazard overlays via the NASA EONET v3 API.

Core Technical Innovations

  1. Mission-Specific Weighting Profiles: Dynamically shifts environmental layer priorities depending on whether an engineer is testing rover traction, cryogenic ice drills, habitat thermal survival, or cave robotics.
  2. Stochastic Monte Carlo Uncertainty Modeling: Executes 4,000-draw stochastic simulations across Earth measurements and planetary targets to output honest p10–p90 confidence bands rather than misleading single-point guarantees.
  3. Institutionalized Scientific Honesty: Explicitly excludes unmeasured layers from the scoring denominator and permanently flags physical limits that Earth cannot replicate (such as lunar vacuum, Martian atmospheric pressure, and reduced gravity).

Project Impact & Future Potential

ArtemisTwin bridges the gap between planetary orbital science and terrestrial field testing. By providing an open, transparent, and reproducible screening tool, it enables space agencies, commercial aerospace teams, and academic researchers to design multi-site testing campaigns, reduce hardware risk, and accelerate humanity's return to the Moon and journey to Mars.

Super Intelligence (SI) Tools & Production Disclosure:

  • Code & Data Processing: OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude were used to assist in developing frontend UI components, interactive map modules, and client-side layout logic. Google DeepMind Antigravity and DeepSeek Harness were used to assist with backend logic, data-processing scripts, analog screening workflows, and the 4,000-draw Monte Carlo simulation pipeline.
  • Research & Technical Writing: Anthropic Claude and Google Gemini were used to synthesize planetary science literature, refine dataset provenance documentation, and structure project descriptions.
  • Video & Multimedia: CapCut was used for final video editing alongside real archival space imagery and live screen recordings of the ArtemisTwin web application. Claude was used for design suggestions.
